input.rationale: Section 6.3 does contain a counterparty-side indemnity: Cellco as Servicer (p0291) and as Marketing Agent (p0292) indemnifies the Issuer and trustees for third-party claims and defence costs, with a standard notice/assumption-of-defence/settlement procedure (p0293-p0295) and survival (p0296-p0298), and there is no one-way indemnity running from our side (p0372 is only a narrow defend-title covenant by the Depositor for claims through the Depositor). However, the indemnity trigger is limited to Cellco's willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence, tracking the liability standard in Section 6.2(a) (p0283). It therefore omits material prongs the rule requires: no third-party intellectual property infringement indemnity at all (which the detection guidance expressly treats as a deviation), no indemnity for Cellco's failure to comply with applicable Law, and none for unauthorized access to or disclosure of Obligor data caused by Cellco — real exposures here given Cellco's consumer-facing servicing and its custody of Obligor personal data. Because the clause fails both the preferred position and the fallback (which still requires an IP indemnity), we propose the minimum addition of a new Section 6.3(a)(iii) adding the IP, breach-of-Law and data-breach prongs, leaving the existing procedure, survival and repayment mechanics untouched.

proposal.summary: Extend Servicer/Marketing Agent indemnity to third-party IP infringement, non-compliance with Law and Cellco-caused data breaches
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We extended Cellco's indemnity in Section 6.3(a) to cover third-party IP infringement claims, failure to comply with Law and unauthorized access to or disclosure of Obligor data, because the current trigger (willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence) leaves the Issuer exposed on claims arising from Cellco's servicing activities and its handling of Obligor data. Our playbook requires these prongs; we can discuss limiting the IP prong to materials and systems Cellco supplies.

ops.text: (iii) In addition, each of the Servicer and the Marketing Agent, severally and not jointly, will defend, indemnify and hold harmless the Indemnified Persons for all fees, expenses, losses, claims, actions, suits, damages and liabilities (including reasonable legal fees and expenses) resulting from any third-party claim to the extent arising out of (A) an allegation that any systems, software, reports or other materials provided or used by the Servicer or the Marketing Agent in performing its obligations under the Transaction Documents infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right, (B) the Servicer's or the Marketing Agent's failure to comply with any Law applicable to it, or (C) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Obligor or Receivable data caused by the Servicer or the Marketing Agent, in each case without regard to whether such conduct constitutes willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence.
